uncited: Mesh Assembly and Data Structure defines the mechanism for aggregating raw geometric primitives (vertices, indices, normals) generated by voxel face culling into contiguous, GPU-ready buffer structures.
It solves the problem of fragmented geometry by consolidating data from disparate voxel blocks or render layers into dense memory regions, optimizing bandwidth and reducing draw call overhead.

It differs from [Block face vertex layout](2374-block-face-vertex-layout.md) and [Voxel Face and Geometry Generation](11724-voxel-face-and-geometry-generation.md) by focusing on the *aggregation* and *buffer management* phase rather than the geometric construction or vertex layout itself.
The family operates on the output of the geometry generation phase, which produces exposed faces as quads.
The core mechanism involves iterating through these quads and packing them into typed, contiguous arrays.

**Layer Separation:** Geometry is often segregated by render layer (e.g., Opaque, Water, Transparent) to allow for correct depth sorting and shader assignment [S2, 4100-chunk-mesh-assembly.md, unofficial].

**Contiguous Buffering:** Vertices and indices are written into flat arrays (`Float32Array`, `Uint32Array`, etc.) to minimize memory fragmentation and facilitate efficient GPU buffer uploads [S2, 4100-chunk-mesh-assembly.md, unofficial].

**Offset Tracking:** For each layer or material section, the assembly process tracks `vertexOffset` and `indexOffset` to ensure that submesh descriptors correctly map to the contiguous data ranges [S2, 4100-chunk-mesh-assembly.md, unofficial].

**Attribute Packing:** Per-vertex attributes (block IDs, lighting, AO) are packed into separate arrays or interleaved formats, often quantized (e.g., normals to `Int8`) to save memory [S2, 4100-chunk-mesh-assembly.md, unofficial].
The specific implementations described in the child articles originate from modern voxel engine development, particularly those targeting web-based or high-performance real-time rendering.

The "Chunk Mesh Assembly" details align with Unreal Engine C++ patterns (`FChunkMeshSection`, `UMaterialInterface`), suggesting a hybrid or engine-agnostic design philosophy [S3, 4100-chunk-mesh-assembly.md, unofficial].
